messages:
jamie: FYI — customer reported embeddings API returning a 400 and wrong vector length when they send a single item. They said it worked in dev but failed in prod. Repro attached, can someone take a look?

lisa: Can you paste the exact request they sent + the server response? even a curl or fetch snippet is fine.

jamie: Here is the curl they sent (customer is using a fetch wrapper that stringifies before sending):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"input":"[0.12,0.05,0.9]","model":"text-embedding-3-small"}'
```

Response they got: 
```json
{
  "error": "Bad Request: embedding input schema invalid",
  "details": "expected array of strings or array of arrays, got string"
}
```

mike: This screams double-stringify. They sent a single precomputed vector (floats) but wrapped it as a JSON string in `input`. Our API expects either a single string (text) or an array-of-strings / array-of-arrays for batch/explicit vectors. A quoted JSON array becomes a string -> our input validation treats it as text, then downstream converters try to interpret and fail.

priya: Saw this a lot with fetch + JSON.stringify layered twice. Example bad pattern:
```js
// BAD: outer code already stringified elsewhere
fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify(vectorArray) })
})
// leads to server receiving input as a string: "[0.1,0.2,...]"
```
Fix is to send the actual array or text:
```js
fetch(url, {
  method:'POST',
  headers:{'Content-Type':'application/json'},
  body: JSON.stringify({ input: vectorArray }) // or input: "the text to embed"
})
```

jamie: Additional wrinkle — customer actually sent numeric vectors (precomputed) but the model they used expects 1536 dims; their vector was 768. They got noisier errors and a billing surprise because they were also sending huge stringified payloads in a tight loop. Billing team flagged a spike.

ingest-bot: alert: embeddings-request-queue spike detected for customer_id=acme-42, avg_payload_size=2.3MB, rate=420 req/min

mike: TL;DR: two separate problems combined — (1) double-encoded input treated as text -> validation error; (2) incorrect vector dims for the selected model -> dimension mismatch/quality failure. Also they were accidentally compressing incorrectly so content-type mismatch made things worse.

lisa: For support playbook: add checklist to ask customers: 1) are you sending an array or a string? 2) paste raw HTTP body (not code wrapper) 3) Content-Type header present? 4) are you sending precomputed vectors or raw text? 5) model you used + expected dims.

mike: Engineering idea: we can improve error messages when we detect a string that parses to a JSON array — suggest: "Input appears to be a JSON-encoded array string; send as a JSON array (no extra quoting) or set input to the string you intend." Should reduce confusion. Filing a small PR.

priya: Also recommending a short doc snippet for client libs: "If you already have a serialized body, don't JSON.stringify again" + quick fetch/axios examples.

lisa: Assigning to @mike to draft the error text PR and @priya to update devex examples. @jamie please send the customer's corrected request so we can confirm billing/throughput normalized. :+1:

jamie: Customer applied fix (sent array instead of quoted string and picked model with matching dims). Confirmed: no more 400s, throughput back to normal, billing spike reduced. I'll close the support case and add the repro to internal KB. Thanks everyone! :relieved:
